answer.evidence: The object is a tiling leaf texture with a bump on top, drawn as one flat vertical mass (rows 17-79, plus the bump in rows 0-16). The only top cue is a 1-2 row light highlight along the upper silhouette (rows 1-3 on the bump, rows 18-19 on the main block). It has no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse, and no visible contents. The same light/dark band repeats every 16 rows down the body (rows 34-35, 50-51, 66-67), which marks tile repetition, not a horizontal surface. Rows 77-79 are a dark base shadow. This is a front elevation of foliage with only a rim at the top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a rectangular canopy block with only 10 distinct colours overall and a median of 7 colours per 16x16 tile. The references have 427 and 567 colours and a median of about 108 per tile, so the candidate is far below both. It breaks up the surface and the 5x5 flat-fill coverage is 0%, but it lacks the varied leaf clumps, bright highlight masses and individually shaded clusters of the references. The outline is a dark green tone with 0% neutral edge pixels, which is correct. The overall look is a flat, uniform, tiled hedge. It has no strong light/dark clump structure, so it reads as thinner and flatter than the references, which have rich canopy lumps with branches and trunk. The density gap is too large to pass.
